title: Packaging a pack without breaking anyone's install

questions.q: Why is pinning numpy==1.24.0 in your pack a problem for others?
options: Pins are not allowed in requirements files
All packs share one Python, so it moves numpy for every pack
It makes your pack load slowly
numpy cannot be installed twice on a card
questions.answer: All packs share one Python, so it moves numpy for every pack
questions.why: There is one environment. Your request applies to everyone in it.

questions.q: Two packs both register a node called Blur. Which one do users get?
options: The last loaded, and the order isn't promised
questions.answer: The last loaded, and the order isn't promised
questions.why: NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS[name] = node_cls runs for each pack, and folders come from os.listdir.

questions.q: A pack tries to register a node named KSampler. What happens?
questions.why: Core's names are passed as ignore to load_custom_node.

questions.q: What does ComfyUI itself do with your requirements.txt when it loads your pack?
options: Refuses to load if it is missing
questions.why: The loader imports your module and has no install step. A person or a manager installs them.

questions.q: Which command shows what would change, and installs nothing?
questions.why: The pip docs: don't actually install anything, just print what would be.

questions.q: Your pack needs cv2 for one node. What is the kindest way to import it?
options: Inside that node's function, with a clear error if it is missing
By running pip from your code
questions.answer: Inside that node's function, with a clear error if it is missing
questions.why: A top-level failure costs the whole pack, while this costs one node.
